title: Japanese-Style Beef Curry with Carrots, Potatoes and a Spiced Roux
summary: A comforting homestyle Japanese curry with fork-tender beef, carrots and potatoes in a rich gravy thickened with a from-scratch spiced butter roux instead of a packet block.
equipment: large heavy pot or casserole (about 5 l) with a lid

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck, cut into 3 cm pieces
carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm pieces
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
apple (about half), peeled and finely grated
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the spice blend
steps.text: Tip the coriander, cumin, turmeric, ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, fenugreek, cayenne and black pepper into the small bowl and stir to combine. Having the blend measured out now means it can go straight into the roux later instead of fumbling with jars while the butter is hot. Set the bowl aside until needed.

steps.title: Brown the beef in batches
steps.text: Pat the beef dry with kitchen paper, then heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the large pot over medium-high heat. Brown half the beef for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until well coloured on most sides, then lift it onto the plate and repeat with the rest. Browning in two batches, rather than crowding the pot, stops the meat steaming in its own juices so it builds a proper crust and deeper flavour.

steps.title: Soften the onions and carrots
steps.text: Add the remaining oil and the onions to the pot, lower the heat to medium-low and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring and scraping up the browned bits stuck to the base. The onions should turn soft and golden; those browned bits are packed with flavour and melt back into the stew. Stir in the carrots and cook for a further 4 minutes to soften their edges.

steps.title: Braise the beef
steps.text: Return the beef and its resting juices to the pot, pour in the stock and water, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the beef is almost tender. The long, slow heat carries the meat well past 63°C, giving the tough connective tissue time to soften.

steps.title: Add potatoes and apple
steps.text: Stir in the potatoes, grated apple, soy sauce and salt, then simmer uncovered for about 20 minutes. It's ready when a knife meets no resistance in the potatoes and a skewer slides easily into the beef, which should now feel fork-tender. The grated apple melts into the sauce as it cooks, adding gentle natural sweetness and body.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: While the stew finishes, melt the butter in the saucepan over medium-low heat, then whisk in the flour. Cook for 10-15 minutes, whisking often and lowering the heat if it colours too fast, until the roux turns a nutty light brown. This slow toasting cooks out the raw flour taste and builds a deep, savoury backbone for the gravy.

steps.title: Season the roux
steps.text: Take the saucepan off the heat and whisk in the grated ginger and the spice blend, stirring for about 1 minute. Working off the heat keeps the spices from scorching in the hot butter, so their aroma stays warm and bright rather than bitter.

steps.title: Thicken the curry
steps.text: Ladle about 250ml of the hot cooking liquid from the pot into the roux, whisking until smooth, then stir it back into the stew. Simmer for 3-5 minutes, stirring and scraping the base, until the sauce turns glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. The beef, braised far beyond the point of being safely cooked through, will be fork-tender throughout.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle the curry over bowls of short-grain rice while it's hot. The sauce should cling thickly to the beef, carrots and potatoes rather than pooling thinly around them.

tips: Pat the beef completely dry before it hits the pan; wet meat steams instead of browning and the stew loses its deep colour.
Watch the roux closely once it starts turning golden — it can go from nutty to burnt within a minute or two, so pull it off the heat early if in doubt.
Grating the apple rather than chopping it lets it melt seamlessly into the sauce, adding sweetness without leaving visible chunks.
Don't rush the braise; the beef needs the full simmering time to become properly fork-tender.
storage: Cool the curry quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; use within 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan until piping hot and the centre reaches 74°C before serving; the potatoes can turn a little softer if the curry has been frozen and thawed. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
